newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Bund vols bid up as FOMC looms.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Bund vols bid up as FOMC looms.

text.p: Implied volatility of Bund options ticked higher on Tuesday with traders describing the market as defensive ahead of a key U.S. monetary policy meeting.
Most of the Bund option activity was centred in call trading, although straddles were also popular, traders said.

"We have seen some defensive activity by the market makers ahead of the FOMC," said a French broker on London's LIFFE floor. "They are not that keen to buy but they don't want to sell too cheaply either."
Implied vol of November options on December Bund futures was quoted at 4.7 percent, up from Monday's closing 4.56 percent.
Further out, in December option vols had also firmed, traders said, while January straddles were being quoted at 5.00 percent implied volatility, up from 4.9 percent on Monday.
"March is very quiet, but the vol there is about 5.1 percent in the middle," the French broker said.
Dealers said one U.S. house had been a big seller of straddles in November options and December straddles had also seen some business.
"On the whole the trade has been in selling calls into any strength (in the underlying Bund market)," said another trader on the LIFFE floor.
December Bund futures were 19 basis points higher at 98.07 by 1055 GMT, having hit a high at 98.09 in early trade.
LIFFE screens showed that almost 3,000 lots of November 98.50 calls had gone through by 1056 GMT, with volume in November 99.00 calls ticking just past the 1,000 lots mark.
The trader said there was some nervousness before the FOMC meeting, but the potential fallout for Bund futures if U.S. rates were raised was not likely to be too drastic.
"We would probably see a quick dip (in the underlying market) with vols bid up for a while," he said. "But things should settle down fairly soon after that."

In a poll by Reuters, 17 out of 30 economists asked said they expected the federal reserve to tighten monetary policy after this meeting, with all but one forecasting a 25 basis point hike in the 5.25 percent federal funds rate.
Analysts were not expecting any decision to emerge until 1800 or 1900 GMT, well after London markets are closed.
